spec_notes: The spec is mostly a list of checks. Its marked 'Default:' lines decide U-29/U-30 (identity, type and reader fields managed by the app; only existing business fields, value types preserved), U-41 (a stopped server leaves tasks interrupted for explicit retry) and token sharing across personas. Several choices are decided only in the architecture note, not marked as choices for the customer: order ids allocated at proposal time (U-32/U-34), one session cookie per browser (U-1), one server per data folder. It is silent on duplicate names (U-9, U-15), conversation naming (U-11), what 'Since you were away' covers (U-44), storage and start-up failures (U-46, U-54, U-57, U-60) and focus (U-58). Nothing in the spec contradicts the request.
tests_notes: TC-1..TC-9 are broad scenario tests that each cover many behaviours (TC-6 covers authorization, clarify, reject, apply-once, stale conflict, invalid readers and restart persistence in one test). TC-7 pins the previewed id to ORD-1005 and TC-9 pins detail text ('Step 2 failed. Retry to continue from this step.'), so another correct build could fail them. Tests use the server's own JSON action protocol (action names, requestId), which is internal. test/browser.cjs (UI-1) is picked up by npm test but registers no test when NODE_TEST_CONTEXT is set, so npm test reports it as passed without running it; it passes when run directly and is tied to element ids and CSS values (border radius, min-width, max-width). No test covers duplicate names, conversation naming, storage failures, damaged data or 'Since you were away'.
maintainer: Every state change goes through one synchronous copy-on-write snapshot of the whole workspace, and the reply path and the task worker both assume store.write never throws once work has started; a write failure there leaves state (a pending reply, a 'Running' task) that only a restart repairs. Behaviour also leans on the stand-in's exact reply texts (the bot says 'Confirm to apply it' for proposals the app refuses), so changing validation means reconciling two voices, and the single all-in-one scenario tests will not localize what broke.
